addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- ecc:a11y-architect: Accessibility Architect specializing in WCAG 2.2 compliance for Web and Native platforms. Use PROACTIVELY when designing UI components, establishing design systems, or auditing code for inclusive user experiences. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)

- ecc:agent-evaluator: Evaluates agent output against 5-axis quality rubric (accuracy, completeness, clarity, actionability, conciseness). Use after any non-trivial task when the user wants a quality assessment, or when the agent-self-evaluation skill is active. Produces structured scorecard with evidence and improvement suggestions. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- ecc:architect: Software architecture specialist for system design, scalability, and technical decision-making. Use PROACTIVELY when planning new features, refactoring large systems, or making architectural decisions. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- ecc:build-error-resolver: Build and TypeScript error resolution specialist. Use PROACTIVELY when build fails or type errors occur. Fixes build/type errors only with minimal diffs, no architectural edits. Focuses on getting the build green quickly. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- ecc:chief-of-staff: Personal communication chief of staff that triages email, Slack, LINE, and Messenger. Classifies messages into 4 tiers (skip/info_only/meeting_info/action_required), generates draft replies, and enforces post-send follow-through via hooks. Use when managing multi-channel communication workflows. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit, Write)

- ecc:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing implementation blueprints with concrete files, interfaces, data flow, and build order. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- ecc:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, and documenting dependencies to inform new development. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- ecc:code-reviewer: Expert code review specialist. Proactively reviews code for quality, security, and maintainability. Use immediately after writing or modifying code. MUST BE USED for all code changes. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- ecc:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving behavior. Focus on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)
- ecc:comment-analyzer: Analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, maintainability, and comment rot risk. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- ecc:conversation-analyzer: Use this agent when analyzing conversation transcripts to find behaviors worth preventing with hooks. Triggered by /hookify without arguments. (Tools: Read, Grep)

- ecc:cpp-build-resolver: C++ build, CMake, and compilation error resolution specialist. Fixes build errors, linker issues, and template errors with minimal changes. Use when C++ builds fail. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob)

- ecc:cpp-reviewer: Expert C++ code reviewer specializing in memory safety, modern C++ idioms, concurrency, and performance. Use for all C++ code changes. MUST BE USED for C++ projects. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- ecc:csharp-reviewer: Expert C# code reviewer specializing in .NET conventions, async patterns, security, nullable reference types, and performance. Use for all C# code changes. MUST BE USED for C# projects. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- ecc:dart-build-resolver: Dart/Flutter build, analysis, and dependency error resolution specialist. Fixes `dart analyze` errors, Flutter compilation failures, pub dependency conflicts, and build_runner issues with minimal, surgical changes. Use when Dart/Flutter builds fail. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

## Session Summary

### Tasks
- Debugged GTK4 transparent background issue in gtk4-widget-factory when GTK3 matugen template was working correctly
- Located and analyzed GTK4 theme configuration files and directories
- Created and integrated GTK4-specific CSS overrides into the matugen theme pipeline
- Fixed accent color rendering in GTK4 widgets

### Decisions Made
- Used CSS widget-level overrides in `gtk.css` rather than relying solely on color variables
- Created a separate `gtk4-overrides.css` matugen template to persist GTK4 fixes across theme regenerations
- Integrated the gtk4-overrides template into `config.toml` so future matugen runs preserve the fixes
- Applied fixes to the user's personal config directories (`~/.config/gtk-4.0/`, `~/.config/matugen/`)

### Files Modified
- `/home/krubics/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css` — added widget-level accent color overrides
- `/home/krubics/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini` — theme configuration updates
- `/home/krubics/.config/matugen/templates/gtk/gtk4-overrides.css` — created new persistent template file
- `/home/krubics/.config/matugen/config.toml` — wired gtk4-overrides template into the pipeline

### Unresolved Issues
- gtk4-widget-factory requires restart to display CSS changes (expected behavior, not a blocker)
- May need further fine-tuning of accent color values depending on visual inspection after restart

### Next Session Context
- GTK4 theming requires both CSS variable definitions AND widget-level color overrides (unlike GTK3)
- Matugen templates for GTK4 should live in `/home/krubics/.config/matugen/templates/gtk/`
- User is maintaining a customized theme using matugen with GTK3/GTK4 parity as a goal
- Accent color handling differs significantly between GTK3 and GTK4; GTK4 uses libadwaita conventions
